name: Black Flag
label: SST
lede: Greg Ginn started SST to put out his own band, Raymond Pettibon gave the band four black bars, and five singers came through in seven years. Ginn kept the name through all of it.

hero.by: Henry Rollins with Black Flag, 1983. Wikimedia Commons

eras.title: Panic in Hermosa Beach
eras.text: Greg Ginn had been running a radio-electronics business since he was 12, and he didn't much like rock music. He started a fast, ugly band anyway, his brother drew it a flag, and when no label would pay for the record, the electronics company became SST Records.

years.h: Ginn and Keith Morris start a band called Panic
years.p: Ginn on guitar and [[Keith Morris|6102710c-0c36-48df-9b95-e01c9264562c]] on vocals start Panic in Hermosa Beach. [[Chuck Dukowski|19a07153-933f-4725-a5de-477cb3554517]] comes in on bass, and [[Robo|6dc378d0-6465-45d3-8b5a-918e2c19b278]] later takes the drum stool from Brian Migdoll.

years.src: Arthur · Wikipedia: Greg Ginn · Wikipedia: Black Flag
years.h: Panic cuts its first session at Media Art, Hermosa Beach
years.p: Bomp! Records wanted the tapes, then ran short of money. Nobody else was offering, so Ginn paid for the record himself.
years.xp:
Ginn wasn't eager to be a label. "I wasn't looking forward to putting out records myself, because I felt that I had my hands full," he told Arthur.

The company he did it through had started as Solid State Tuners, the electronics business Ginn ran as a ham-radio kid. As SST Records it went on to release [[Minutemen|d4ad0149-d8ae-4105-8009-0221fce9ff35]], [[Hüsker Dü|5c4c90a4-539f-4101-83cf-301bc6a94e06]], [[Meat Puppets|3df040ee-2b8b-446b-937a-3f86f4b2cabf]], [[Descendents|f035837e-4117-438d-a524-cacf43500e68]], [[Sonic Youth|5cbef01b-cc35-4f52-af7b-d0df0c4f61b9]] and [[Soundgarden|153c9281-268f-4cf3-8938-f5a4593e5df4]].

years.h: Raymond Pettibon renames Panic and draws four black bars
years.p: Another band already had the name Panic. Ginn's brother [[Raymond Pettibon|3e603b97-d5f8-4547-891b-74cdfd2ed7bf]] offered Black Flag and a logo: four bars, a flag caught mid-ripple.
years.xp:
The name worked three ways: the opposite of a white flag of surrender, the anarchist banner, and a brand of bug spray. Pettibon's pen-and-ink panels went on to cover nearly every flyer, sleeve, shirt and skateboard the band put out into the early 1980s.

Arthur reports that Ginn was arrested on a flyering run in Redondo Beach, and that after his court date he and Dukowski spray-painted the bars on the police station wall.

years.h: Black Flag's first show is at a Moose Lodge in Redondo Beach
years.p: The first advertised show under the new name, in a fraternal lodge. Morris swings from the flags over the stage, gets chased off by the lodge's veterans, and comes back for the second set in a black wig.

years.h: Nervous Breakdown: SST 001, 2,000 copies for $1,000
years.p: Four songs in about five minutes, the first record on Ginn's label. Pettibon's cover: a man backed against a wall, fists up.

yt: Black Flag live at Polliwog Park, 1979
years.h: Manhattan Beach picnickers throw their lunch at the band
years.p: The band fills a slot at a family concert in a city park. The parents on blankets answer with food.
years.xp:
The slot had been the US Air Force Orchestra's. Asked what kind of music the band played, Ginn told the parks official, "it's got a little bit of jazz, but it's rock."

By the end an official was pleading, "You guys have to stop!" The Parks Department's press release afterward: "We plan to screen and audition every act from now on."

years.src: Center Label · Arthur · Wikipedia: Ron Reyes
years.h: Morris out, Ron Reyes in at Blackie's
years.p: Morris quits after the October sessions and starts the [[Circle Jerks|22995eba-1238-4b4f-a937-ac2c5767ab9f]]. [[Ron Reyes|d065eb41-b9e7-42cb-b2a5-6d211aa328e2]], a 19-year-old Kiss fan who already knows every song, debuts at Blackie's in Los Angeles.
years.xp: Morris has been frank about the shape he was in. "I'd become pretty much like a monkey let to run loose," he told Arthur. Reyes went straight from Blackie's into a run of shows in Vancouver.

eras.title: The cops, the closet and the kid from D.C.
eras.text: In two years the band burned through two singers, got named in the Los Angeles Times as the face of punk violence, and had police waiting at soundcheck. It ended with Henry Rollins on the mic, an album in the can and a record company that wouldn't touch it.

yt: 'Depression' in The Decline of Western Civilization
years.h: Reyes lives in a closet at the Church, and shows it on film
years.p: In Penelope Spheeris's The Decline of Western Civilization, Reyes shows off where he sleeps: a closet in the Church, the old Hermosa Beach Baptist church the band used as a practice room.

years.src: Center Label · Wikipedia: List of Black Flag · Wikipedia: Ron Reyes
years.h: Reyes walks off mid-set at the Fleetwood, Redondo Beach
years.p: Sick of the violence in the pit, Reyes leaves the stage. Audience members take turns singing, he comes back, then quits for good that night.
years.xp:
"I felt, 'What's the point?'... So I just walked offstage," Reyes said later. He still came back to record the Jealous Again EP, credited as Chavo Pederast.

Two weeks later, on June 6, Morris was back singing at the Fleetwood. Reyes moved to Vancouver and formed Crash Bang Crunch Pop! He'd be back in 2013.

years.src: Arthur · Center Label · Wikipedia: Black Flag
years.h: The Los Angeles Times runs 'Violence Sneaks Into Punk Scene'
years.p: The feature ties Black Flag to punk violence. The LAPD under Chief Daryl Gates starts treating the band's shows as trouble to be stopped.
years.xp:
In October 1980 county sheriffs cleared fans from a Whisky show, bottles flew and the club's manager was fired; Ginn said the LAPD had made the call. In November, police set up a command post across from Baces Hall during soundcheck, with helicopters overhead.

Arthur describes a January 1981 show that ran up $4,000 in damage and ended with an LAPD motorcycle officer hit by a car. "We were pouring our aggression into the music, we were NOT acting it out," Dukowski said.

years.h: Dez Cadena, Red Cross's guitarist, becomes singer number three
years.p: [[Dez Cadena|f3cd8685-7490-44ee-a5bd-cc6663ea1396]] takes the mic and sings on the Six Pack EP and the band's 'Louie Louie' single.

years.h: Hermosa Beach police raid SST the morning after the band leaves
years.p: With the band gone on tour, police hit the SST office. [[Mike Watt|568203ae-c27b-4990-8997-09c0d5c0de77]] of [[Minutemen|d4ad0149-d8ae-4105-8009-0221fce9ff35]] is there and ends up paying a $50 zoning fine.
years.xp:
A Hermosa Beach cop told Dukowski, "There's a stack of law books from here to the beach. I can do anything I want." Arthur says Ginn was also arrested for assault after throwing coffee at an official at a La Mirada High School show.

On the road the per diem was $5 when there was one, and shows paid $50 to $100. Mail-order records paid the bills, and for a stretch the band lived in a storage unit.

years.cap: The new line-up behind the Cuckoo's Nest, 1981
years.src: Center Label · Wikipedia: Henry Rollins · Arthur
years.h: A Häagen-Dazs manager from D.C. gets up to sing at A7
years.p: After Black Flag's Irving Plaza show, [[Henry Rollins|656b39fb-979c-4c57-bb87-61d1a8eb38d1]] of D.C.'s [[SOA|e54cb250-3502-4c32-9482-70488bd9a8cb]] sings 'Clocked In' with the band at the A7 afterparty. They ask him to audition.
years.xp:
Cadena's voice was shot and he wanted to play guitar. Rollins auditioned at Tu Casa Studio, then quit Häagen-Dazs, sold his car and moved west. He met the band in Detroit on July 14, roadied the rest of the tour and sang encores.

His first show as singer was at the Cuckoo's Nest in Costa Mesa. "I thought I was ready... Greg Ginn taught me otherwise," Rollins told Arthur.

years.h: Damaged: $8,500, under three weeks, a fist through a mirror
years.p: The band's first album, with 'Rise Above', 'TV Party' and 'Six Pack', cut at Unicorn Studios on Santa Monica Boulevard. Ed Colver shot Rollins punching a mirror for the cover.
years.xp: Colver had already cracked the mirror with a hammer. The blood was red ink and coffee. [[Kurt Cobain|3c9b356d-d1db-4f4e-a7a3-2d00c1d70255]] later put Damaged on his list of his fifty favorite albums.

years.big: "I'm not the kind of guy who believes in burning books"
years.h: MCA's president won't distribute Damaged
years.p: MCA's Al Bergamo pulls the record from Unicorn Records' distribution deal. The band stickers his own words on 25,000 copies and sells it through independents.
years.xp:
Bergamo's full statement: "this record bothered me. As a parent with two children, I found it an anti-parent record, past the point of good taste."

The band's sticker quoted him back: "As a parent ... I found it an anti-parent record."

years.h: Robo can't get back into the country after the UK tour
years.p: Colombian-born drummer [[Robo|6dc378d0-6465-45d3-8b5a-918e2c19b278]] hits visa trouble at the end of the band's December 1981 UK tour and can't legally return to the US. He later drums for the [[Misfits|936addc3-91aa-49de-8ec0-0dc186de151f]].

eras.title: A band barred from its own name
eras.text: For two years a court order kept Black Flag from releasing records as Black Flag. So the band stayed in the practice room, went through drummers, singers and a founding bassist, and came out slower and heavier.

years.h: Three drummers in a year: Emil Johnson, Chuck Biscuits, Bill Stevenson
years.p: Emil Johnson, 16, quits mid-tour after a fight with roadie Mugger. [[D.O.A.|0f0b2f97-a073-4a92-ab99-ff7980ad7fca]]'s [[Chuck Biscuits|2ba59002-1ff3-4f53-87aa-6a085acf15e2]] won't do the rehearsal schedule. [[Bill Stevenson|328e3ae5-7d8c-4a01-b2b3-b8f41fb7bb23]] of the [[Descendents|f035837e-4117-438d-a524-cacf43500e68]] will.

years.h: Everything Went Black, with the band's name papered over
years.p: Old recordings with all three pre-Rollins singers. Wherever the artwork said Black Flag, small slips of paper covered it, because Unicorn Records had a court order.
years.xp:
Unicorn sued for breach of contract after the Damaged mess and won an injunction barring the band from recording under its own name. Ginn and Dukowski served several days in Los Angeles County Jail for contempt of court.

The case only ended when Unicorn went out of business.

years.h: Cadena leaves to start DC3
years.p: Cadena goes off to front his own band. The band doesn't replace him and carries on with one guitar.

years.h: Rollins hits a fan in England; Ginn calls him macho
years.p: At a show in England, Rollins goes after an audience member who attacked Ginn. The thanks he gets: Ginn calls him a "macho asshole."
years.xp: Fans were attacking Rollins most nights by then, and he fought back, dragging people onstage. Before shows he paced in black shorts, grinding his teeth and squeezing a pool ball.

years.cap: Rollins, with Roessler on bass, Berlin
years.src: Wikipedia: Black Flag · Wikipedia: List of Black Flag
years.h: Rollins fires Dukowski; Kira Roessler gets the bass
years.p: Ginn was unhappy with Dukowski's playing, and Wikipedia says Rollins took it on himself to fire him. Dukowski stays on as manager. L.A. punk veteran [[Kira Roessler|2c65be73-5658-47c5-9619-01f78db0e2cb]] joins after the My War sessions.

eras.title: Slower, longer, meaner
eras.text: Free of Unicorn, the band put out three albums in 1984 alone and played more than 170 shows that year. The slow half of My War cost them hardcore kids and won them a generation in Seattle.

years.h: Side two of My War crawls for nearly twenty minutes
years.p: Ginn plays bass as 'Dale Nixon'. Side two is three songs, all over six minutes: 'Nothing Left Inside', 'Three Nights' and 'Scream'.
years.xp:
Recorded in December 1983 at Total Access in Redondo Beach, with Dukowski's title track still on it. "We want people to listen to us as a band rather than as a stereotype," Ginn said. Rollins on the metal charge: "Take the 'metal' out of 'heavy metal' and that's what we are."

Mudhoney's Steve Turner: "that record instantly made the Melvins slow down to a crawl."

years.h: Rollins reads poetry on one side of Family Man
years.p: Rollins reads spoken word on side one; Ginn's band plays instrumentals on side two. Ginn later said Rollins "got into the serious way-out poet thing."

years.cap: Ginn, Rollins, Roessler and Stevenson, Berlin, June 1984
yt: Live at The Stone, San Francisco, August 1984
years.h: Black Flag plays Seattle, and the future of grunge is in the room
years.p: At the Mountaineer Club, with Green River opening, the crowd includes [[Kurt Cobain|3c9b356d-d1db-4f4e-a7a3-2d00c1d70255]] and [[Melvins|9ccfbc94-a4f4-42f7-b6f5-d903ab77cccb]] leader [[Buzz Osborne|9a911b22-f972-44ee-b2d3-d41297fe96e9]], per Louder.
years.xp: Louder's account, drawn from Michael Azerrad's Come As You Are, puts [[Chris Cornell|cbf9738d-8f81-4a92-bc64-ede09341652d]] and [[Kim Thayil|dd676aae-658e-42f3-b3d9-8660ea29198d]] there too. Seattle didn't mind the slow songs. "A lot of other people around the country hated the fact that Black Flag slowed down," Steve Turner said, "but up here it was really great."

years.h: Roessler has notes on the Slip It In cover
years.p: Cut in June at Total Access with Roessler and Stevenson. Pettibon's cover shows a nun embracing a bare male leg; Roessler's verdict: "That cover does not glorify women."

years.src: Wikipedia: Black Flag · Wikipedia: Loose Nut
years.h: Loose Nut uses Pettibon's drawing without telling him
years.p: Ginn digs out an old Pettibon drawing and hands it to Stevenson for the layout. Ginn never mentioned it to his brother.

years.src: Wikipedia: List of Black Flag · Wikipedia: Black Flag
years.h: Ginn fires Stevenson, then Roessler
years.p: Stevenson is out in late April and goes back to the [[Descendents|f035837e-4117-438d-a524-cacf43500e68]]; Anthony Martinez takes the drums. Roessler is fired in September and C'el Revuelta takes the bass.
years.xp: Wikipedia says Ginn and Rollins cited erratic behavior when they let Roessler go. She married Watt and played with him as Dos.

years.h: In My Head is the last studio album for 28 years
years.p: Metallic and bluesy, cut by Ginn, Rollins, Roessler and Stevenson before that lineup came apart.

years.h: Detroit gets the last show, and nobody says so
years.p: The final tour, January to June with Revuelta and Martinez, ends in Detroit. Nobody announces it's the end.

years.big: "So in one short phone call, it was all over."
q: Henry became such a powerful image that it dissolved the band.
years.h: Ginn phones Rollins to quit his own band
years.p: Rollins found it strange, "considering it was his band and all." He had the [[Rollins Band|3ca37f23-fdce-49ce-86e2-134c9a17ebc5]] going within months.
years.xp:
Ginn's reason: "The underground made a transformation, and I didn't think that [Black Flag] was rooted enough to go through that." He also said the band's range had narrowed to fit "Henry's increasingly narrow 'persona'."

In 2012 Rollins told Scam he had "zero good memories" of his five years in the band.

eras.title: The van becomes a book
eras.text: Rollins turned five years of journals into the Black Flag story most fans know. Ginn's answer, years later, was a reunion: benefit shows for a cat rescue.

years.src: Wikipedia: Get in the Van · Rolling Stone Australia · Goodreads
years.h: Rollins publishes Get in the Van
years.p: Rollins's Black Flag journals, spring 1981 to July 12, 1986, published by his own 2.13.61. The audiobook wins the 1995 Grammy for Best Spoken Word Album.
years.xp:
The cover photo is LAPD officers at a Black Flag show on November 17, 1984. Rolling Stone Australia summed up the book as "a band of antisocial maniacs who hate each other crammed in a van."

One line from the diaries: "I'm constantly around people that talk a lot but say nothing. A sad case."

yt: Live at the Hollywood Palladium, September 12, 2003
years.h: Black Flag reunites for a cat rescue benefit
years.p: Ginn, Cadena, Robo and Revuelta play two Hollywood Palladium nights and Alex's Bar in Long Beach. Per Stereogum, a second set of all of My War had [[Mike Vallely|686467eb-5399-4c43-adbe-dad0e059c738]] singing over pre-recorded bass.

eras.title: Two Black Flags and a lawsuit
eras.text: Thirty years on, two bands claimed the bars: Ginn's Black Flag and FLAG, made of nearly everyone else. It went to federal court, and Ginn's returning singer got pulled offstage in Perth.

years.cap: Reyes and Ginn, Cambridge, Mass., June 2013
years.h: Ginn brings back Ron Reyes; everyone else becomes FLAG
years.p: Ginn announces a new Black Flag with [[Ron Reyes|d065eb41-b9e7-42cb-b2a5-6d211aa328e2]] singing. Morris, Dukowski, Stevenson, Stephen Egerton and Cadena answer with FLAG.
years.xp:
FLAG grew out of a December 2011 Goldenvoice 30th-anniversary show in Santa Monica, where Morris, Dukowski, Stevenson and Egerton played the whole Nervous Breakdown EP.

Ginn's website called FLAG a "fake" band playing in an "embarrassingly weak 'mailing it in' fashion." Morris, in Rolling Stone: "I could just go down a list of people that have sued him and people that have not received royalties."

years.h: SST and Ginn sue FLAG, Rollins and Morris
years.p: The suit claims the name and the four bars. In October a federal judge refuses Ginn an injunction, saying the logo may be in generic use and fans can tell the bands apart.

years.src: Music Feeds · The Line of Best Fit · Wikipedia: Black Flag
years.h: Vallely takes Reyes's mic mid-set in Perth
years.p: Two songs from the end of the Australian tour, manager Vallely walks on and tells Reyes, "You're done, party's over get off." Vallely finishes the set and is named singer in January 2014.
years.xp:
Reyes, on Facebook: "The writing was on the wall since before we played our first show." Raising problems, he wrote, was treated as "a blasphemous stab in the back to Greg," and he would not treat Ginn as "an infallable Pope figure."

He signed off without much malice: "Come on folks it's only rock n roll."

years.h: Reyes draws the cover for What The...
years.p: The first Black Flag album in 28 years, with a cover drawn by Reyes. Critics were rough on it: 42 on Metacritic.
years.xp: Exclaim! described the cover as "a South Park character giving us the devil horns after getting juiced off a bag of Fun Dip." The A.V. Club went with "downright hideous." The same critics had kind words for Reyes's singing.

years.h: One Victimology Tour, then Ginn shelves the band again
years.p: Ginn and Vallely tour with Tyler Smith and Brandon Pertzborn, and the band goes quiet for five years.

eras.title: Tacos, My War and a new voice
eras.text: Ginn keeps bringing the bars back, now with players decades younger. The record that once cost the band its audience became the whole set, and in 2025, after 49 years, a woman took the mic.

years.h: The comeback gig is at a craft beer and taco festival
years.p: Ginn and Vallely return at the Sabroso Craft Beer, Taco & Music Festival. In October they play the UK for the first time in 35 years.

years.h: Black Flag tours North America playing My War in full
years.p: The 1984 album, slow side and all, becomes the nightly set.

years.src: Wikipedia: Black Flag · Wikipedia: List of Black Flag
years.h: Vallely quits; Max Zanelly becomes the first woman to front Black Flag
years.p: Vallely leaves in January after almost 11 years, the longest any singer lasted. Ginn's new lineup: Max Zanelly on vocals, David Rodriguez on bass, Bryce Weston on drums.
